# Episia
> Open-source Python library for epidemiological surveillance, modeling, and biostatistics.
> Designed for resource-limited settings, particularly sub-Saharan Africa.
> Validated against OpenEpi (gold standard in epidemiology).

- Source: https://github.com/Xcept-Health/episia
- Docs: https://episia.readthedocs.io
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/episia/
- Preprint: https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.17.26350337
- DOI (software): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19429374
- License: MIT
- Python: 3.9+
- Version: 0.1.1

## Installation

```bash
pip install episia
pip install episia[full]   # with all optional dependencies
pip install episia[jupyter] # Jupyter + interactive widgets
pip install episia[export]  # PNG/SVG/PDF export via kaleido
```

## Entry point

```python
from episia import epi  # unified convenience singleton
```

## Epidemic modeling — episia.models

Classes: SIRModel, SEIRModel, SEIRDModel, ModelCalibrator, SensitivityAnalysis, ScenarioRunner

```python
from episia.models import SEIRModel
from episia.models.parameters import SEIRParameters

params = SEIRParameters(
    N=1_000_000, I0=10, E0=50,
    beta=0.35,
    sigma=1/5.2,   # 1 / incubation period (days)
    gamma=1/14,    # 1 / infectious period (days)
    t_span=(0, 365),
)
result = SEIRModel(params).run()
print(result.r0)                          # basic reproduction number
print(result.peak_infected)               # peak infected count
result.plot().show()                      # interactive Plotly figure
result.plot(backend="matplotlib")         # publication-quality figure

# via unified API
result = epi.seir(N=1_000_000, I0=10, E0=50, beta=0.35, sigma=1/5.2, gamma=1/14).run()
```

```python
# SEIRD (with mortality)
from episia.models import SEIRDModel
from episia.models.parameters import SEIRDParameters

params = SEIRDParameters(N=1_000_000, I0=1, E0=10, beta=0.35, sigma=1/5.2, gamma=0.09, mu=0.01)
result = SEIRDModel(params).run()
print(result.compartments["D"][-1])       # total deaths
```

```python
# Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis
from episia.models import SensitivityAnalysis

sa = SensitivityAnalysis(
    model_class=SEIRModel,
    param_class=SEIRParameters,
    fixed=dict(N=1_000_000, I0=10, E0=50, t_span=(0, 365)),
    distributions={
        "beta":  ("uniform",    0.25, 0.50),
        "sigma": ("normal",     1/5.2, 0.02),
        "gamma": ("triangular", 1/21, 1/14, 1/7),
    },
    n_samples=500,
    seed=42,
)
sa_result = sa.run()
sa_result.plot("I").show()
print(sa_result.summary())
```

```python
# Multi-scenario comparison
from episia.models.parameters import SEIRParameters, ScenarioSet
from episia.models import ScenarioRunner

scenarios = ScenarioSet([
    ("No intervention", SEIRParameters(N=1_000_000, I0=10, E0=50, beta=0.35, sigma=1/5.2, gamma=1/14)),
    ("50% reduction",   SEIRParameters(N=1_000_000, I0=10, E0=50, beta=0.18, sigma=1/5.2, gamma=1/14)),
    ("70% reduction",   SEIRParameters(N=1_000_000, I0=10, E0=50, beta=0.11, sigma=1/5.2, gamma=1/14)),
])
sr = ScenarioRunner(SEIRModel).run(scenarios)
sr.plot(compartment="I").show()
```

```python
# Model calibration on observed data
from episia.models import ModelCalibrator

calibrator = ModelCalibrator(
    model_class=SEIRModel,
    observed_data=df,           # pandas DataFrame with a "cases" column
    target_column="cases",
)
fitted_params = calibrator.fit(
    initial_params=SEIRParameters(N=1_500_000, beta=0.3, sigma=1/5.2, gamma=1/14),
    bounds={"beta": (0.1, 0.8), "gamma": (1/21, 1/7)},
)
print(fitted_params.r0)
```

## Biostatistics — episia.stats

Functions: risk_ratio, odds_ratio, proportion_ci, mean_ci, incidence_rate,
diagnostic_test_2x2, roc_analysis, sample_size_risk_ratio,
sample_size_single_proportion, mantel_haenszel_or,
logistic_regression, poisson_regression

```python
from episia.stats import risk_ratio, odds_ratio, proportion_ci, diagnostic_test_2x2, roc_analysis, sample_size_risk_ratio

# 2x2 contingency table: a=exposed+case, b=exposed+control, c=unexposed+case, d=unexposed+control
rr = risk_ratio(a=40, b=10, c=20, d=30)
print(rr)               # Risk Ratio: 2.667 (1.514-4.696)
print(rr.significant)   # True
print(rr.p_value)

or_ = odds_ratio(a=40, b=10, c=20, d=30)
print(or_)              # Odds Ratio: 6.000 (2.453-14.678)

# Proportion confidence intervals (5 methods: wilson, wald, jeffreys, clopper-pearson, agresti-coull)
p = proportion_ci(k=45, n=200, method="wilson")
print(p)                # Proportion: 0.2250 (0.1714-0.2888)

# Diagnostic test evaluation
diag = diagnostic_test_2x2(tp=80, fp=10, fn=20, tn=90)
print(diag.sensitivity)   # 0.800
print(diag.specificity)   # 0.900
print(diag.ppv)           # 0.889
print(diag.npv)           # 0.818
print(diag.lr_plus)       # 8.000
print(diag.youden)        # 0.700

# ROC curve and AUC
import numpy as np
roc = roc_analysis(
    y_true=np.array([1,1,1,0,0,0,1,0,1,0]),
    y_score=np.array([0.9,0.8,0.7,0.3,0.2,0.1,0.6,0.4,0.85,0.35])
)
print(roc.auc)
roc.plot().show()

# Sample size for cohort study (risk ratio)
ss = sample_size_risk_ratio(rr_expected=2.0, p0=0.10, alpha=0.05, power=0.80)
print(ss.per_group)     # 199
print(ss.total)         # 398

# Stratified Mantel-Haenszel analysis
from episia.stats.stratified import mantel_haenszel_or
from episia.stats.contingency import Table2x2

strata = [Table2x2(15, 5, 25, 20), Table2x2(30, 10, 40, 35), Table2x2(20, 8, 30, 25)]
mh = mantel_haenszel_or(strata)
print(mh)  # pooled OR, Cochran Q, I²
```

## Visualization — episia.viz

Backends: plotly (default, interactive) or matplotlib (publication-quality, 300 DPI)
Themes: scientific, minimal, dark, colorblind

```python
from episia.viz import plot_epicurve, set_theme

set_theme("dark")   # or "scientific", "minimal", "colorblind"

# Epidemic curve
from episia.api.results import TimeSeriesResult
ts = TimeSeriesResult(times=result.t, values=result.compartments["I"])
plot_epicurve(ts, animate=True).show()

# Export
fig = result.plot(backend="matplotlib")
fig.savefig("figure1.pdf", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
result.plot().write_html("figure1.html")
```

## Surveillance data — episia.data

Classes: SurveillanceDataset, AlertEngine

```python
from episia.data import SurveillanceDataset, AlertEngine

# Load from CSV (DHIS2-compatible)
ds = SurveillanceDataset.from_csv(
    "cases.csv",
    date_col="date", cases_col="cases",
    deaths_col="deaths", district_col="district",
    population_col="population",
)
print(ds.total_cases)
print(ds.total_deaths)

ar = ds.attack_rate(population=500_000, per=100_000)
weekly = ds.aggregate(freq="W")
channel = ds.endemic_channel(percentiles=(25, 50, 75))

# Alert detection (threshold, z-score, endemic channel)
engine = AlertEngine(ds)
alerts = engine.run(threshold=15, zscore_threshold=2.0, use_endemic_channel=True)
summary = engine.alert_summary(alerts)
print(summary["n_alerts"], summary["severity_counts"])
```

## DHIS2 integration — episia.dhis2

Classes: DHIS2Client, DHIS2Adapter

```python
from episia.dhis2 import DHIS2Client, DHIS2Adapter

client = DHIS2Client(
    base_url="https://dhis2.moh.gov.bf",
    username="epi_officer",
    password="...",
)
print(client.about())

cases_data = client.get_data_values(
    data_element="rQLFQyPSmie",
    period="202401:202412",
    org_units="ImspD0yaksKo",
)

adapter = DHIS2Adapter()
ds = adapter.to_surveillance_dataset(cases_data, date_col="period", cases_col="value")
```

## Report generation — episia.api.reporting

Classes: EpiReport, report_from_model

```python
from episia import EpiReport, report_from_model
import webbrowser, os

# Auto-generate from model result
report = report_from_model(
    model_result,
    title="SEIR Analysis - Burkina Faso 2024",
    author="Dr. F. A. S. Ouedraogo",
    institution="Xcept-Health",
)
path = report.save_html("report.html")
webbrowser.open(f"file:///{os.path.abspath(path)}")

# Custom epidemiological bulletin
report = EpiReport(title="Weekly Bulletin - Week 12", author="MOH", institution="Ministry of Health")
report.add_text("Summary text here.", title="Summary")
report.add_metrics({"Cases": 42, "Deaths": 3, "CFR": "7.1%"})
report.add_figure(fig, title="Epidemic curve", caption="Centre Region, 2024.")
report.add_divider()

# Multiple export formats
report.save_html("bulletin.html")
report.save_markdown("bulletin.md")
report.save_json("bulletin.json")

# via unified API
report = epi.report(result, title="SEIR Burkina Faso 2024")
report.save_html("report.html")
```

## Terminal loader for long operations

```python
from episia.core.utilities import EpiLoader

with EpiLoader("Running SEIR model"):
    result = model.run()
```

## Terminal quick reference

```bash
python -m episia
```

## Module structure

- episia.api — unified epi singleton, result objects, reporting
- episia.models — SIR, SEIR, SEIRD, calibration, scenarios, Monte Carlo
- episia.stats — contingency, descriptive, diagnostic, sample size, stratified, regression
- episia.viz — Plotly + Matplotlib backends, themes, epicurve, ROC, forest plots
- episia.data — SurveillanceDataset, AlertEngine, endemic channel
- episia.dhis2 — DHIS2Client, DHIS2Adapter
- episia.core — validator, calculator, exceptions, EpiLoader, constants

## Key design principles

- Every function returns a rich, serializable result object (EpiResult subclass)
- Dual visualization backend: plotly (interactive) and matplotlib (publication-quality)
- 100% offline — zero network dependencies at runtime
- Validated against OpenEpi reference implementation
- Self-contained HTML reports with dark/light mode toggle
